items.title: Israeli MP invokes internment of Japanese Americans in call to restrict Palestinian citizens
items.content:
Israeli MP invokes internment of Japanese Americans in call to restrict Palestinian citizens
Submitted by
Nadav Rapaport
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 11:37
Likud lawmaker Eli Goldschmidt draws parallels with the mass incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II, prompting accusations of unrestrained incitement against Palestinians in Israel
Demonstrators gathered in the Carmel Center for a protest calling for the formation of a new Israeli government that includes Arab political parties (Jess Flom/JNA Press/Sipa USA via Reuters)
Off
An
Israeli
MP from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party has invoked the mass incarceration of people of Japanese descent in the United States during World War II while discussing how Palestinian citizens of Israel should be treated.
“When the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbour, President Roosevelt signed an order to place all citizens of Japanese descent in internment camps. How is that different from our situation?” newly elected Knesset member Eli Goldschmidt
told Channel 14 News
on Sunday.
“We are still at war. We have not yet finished dealing with Hamas; we have Arab terrorism in Judea and Samaria [the occupied West Bank] and problems in southern Lebanon,” Goldschmidt added.
“We cannot allow people who are relatives of those who want to destroy us to be privy to confidential information,” the Likud MP said, referring to Palestinian lawmakers from Ra’am and the Joint List.
Goldschmidt was referring to the controversial executive order signed by US President Franklin D Roosevelt in 1942, which forced the relocation and incarceration of more than 100,000 people of Japanese descent, most of them US citizens.
Palestinian citizens of Israel
are descendants of Palestinians who remained in their homeland after the 1948 Nakba, during which Zionist militias expelled around 750,000 Palestinians to establish the State of Israel.
Despite being granted Israeli citizenship, they have long faced discrimination and incitement.
They number around two million, accounting for approximately 20 percent of Israel’s population.
Since the Palestinian-led Ra’am and Joint List parties won a historic 19 seats in the Knesset in last month’s elections, Netanyahu and his allies have led a campaign of incitement against Palestinians in Israel, portraying the two parties as “terrorism supporters” in an effort to prevent the formation of a government reliant on their backing.
Violence against Palestinians inside Israel has since increased. Last week, a mosque in the village of Ed-Dahi, near Afula, was set on fire in a suspected
arson attack
linked to an Israeli mob.
'Unrestrained incitement'
Later in the interview, Goldschmidt appeared to distance himself from Roosevelt’s executive order, while maintaining that “a democracy at war should prioritise the security consideration”.
“Roosevelt went too far, but the principle of standing firm on security priorities is right for a country in a state of war,” he
said
.
'It is difficult to comprehend just how far the incitement in Likud has gone, and how it continues to escalate without any restraint'
- Yousef Jabareen, Joint List leader
“I am not recommending that we do what Roosevelt did, but I do suggest not relying on Arab parties in forming a government during wartime.”
Since anti-Netanyahu parties won 67 Knesset seats in the elections, opposition parties, including those led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, have been scrambling to form a new government. However, right-wing parties within the bloc have refused to rely on Ra’am and the Joint List.
Yousef Jabareen, leader of the Joint List,
condemned
Goldschmidt’s remarks, writing in a post on X: “It is difficult to comprehend just how far the incitement in Likud has gone, and how it continues to escalate without any restraint.”
Jabareen said Goldschmidt was “effectively calling for placing all Arab citizens in the country in internment camps”, describing the remarks as “shocking statements”.
“We must not remain silent in the face of this incitement, and above all, they must not remain in power for even one more day. They are an existential threat to all of us,” the Palestinian leader said, referring to the Likud-led government.
48 Palestinians

items.title: Ukraine claims drone attack that sank Russian warship at Libyan naval base
items.content:
Ukraine claims drone attack that sank Russian warship at Libyan naval base
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 10:30
Zelensky said seven Ukrainian sea drones struck the corvette at the Benghazi naval base, while the UN called for an independent investigation
Satellite image shows a capsized Russian ship at Benghazi port after a suspected drone strike in eastern Libya, 22 November 2026 (Vantor/AFP)
Off
Ukraine has claimed responsibility for sinking a
Russian
warship at a naval base in eastern
Libya
, in a major expansion of its maritime campaign against Moscow that has brought the nearly five-year war into the Mediterranean.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones to attack the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi Naval Base on Sunday.
The attack, which took place about 2,400km from Ukraine's front line, was among Kyiv's most far-reaching operations against Russian naval assets since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
“Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky said in a post on X on Monday.
“We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he added.
Ukraine's internal security agency, known as the SBU, described the operation as “unique”, saying the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which it accused Moscow of using to transport military equipment.
The SBU said the naval drones were launched from a “mothership” near the target and that Russian forces attempted to intercept them using air, sea and land defences.
Why Russia remains stubbornly insignificant to the Middle East
Read More »
“Ukraine's defence forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea,” the agency said.
Two Libyan military officials said that the strike severely damaged the corvette and triggered a fire at the naval base, AP reported.
They said at least four drones had been intercepted, while two struck the vessel.
Satellite imagery released by Vantor showed the ship capsized at the port after the explosion.
The Guardian also reported that satellite images indicated the vessel had sunk.
A Libyan official said that at least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded.
The country's eastern-based authorities said emergency crews extinguished the fire.
Call for investigation
The strike has raised concerns about the growing involvement of Libya in the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, particularly amid reports that Ukrainian military personnel and drone specialists have been operating in the country's western regions.
The eastern-based Libyan government said the Merkury had docked at Benghazi to refuel and take on supplies while returning to Russia under a cooperation agreement with the administration.
Russia ties Black Sea grain deal with Ukraine to halt in oil refinery strikes
Read More »
Osama Hammad, head of the eastern-based government, said he had requested an international investigation through the UN General Assembly and Security Council.
The United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) expressed “serious concern” over the attacks at Benghazi port and off the city's coast, calling for an immediate investigation.
“Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the mission said in a statement on Sunday.
It called for an “immediate, independent and transparent investigation” to establish what happened and hold those responsible to account.
Libya has been divided between rival administrations for over a decade, following the 2011 uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi.
The internationally recognised Government of National Unity, led by Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, is based in Tripoli and controls much of the west.
A rival administration operates in the east, backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar and his Libyan National Army, which has maintained ties with Russia.

items.title: Israeli army demolishes one of the last Palestinian communities in Jordan Valley
items.content:
Israeli army demolishes one of the last Palestinian communities in Jordan Valley
The Israeli army has destroyed one of the last Palestinian communities in the Jordan Valley in the occupied West Bank.
Khirbet Samra, a Palestinian Bedouin herding community, had all structures and infrastructure demolished in an army operation on Sunday.
Alon Cohen of Bimkom – Planners for Planning Rights told Haaretz that the demolition had been "cruel and illegal."
"Most of the structures and the electricity and water systems had no demolition orders at all. Furthermore, there were five orders issued about 17 years ago, and no structure could be demolished based on them," he said.

items.title: Trump administration deported US citizen to Mexico, DoJ admits in court
items.content:
Brian Morales García of Texas seeks damages after he was wrongly identified as undocumented in case White House wants dropped
The
Trump administration
recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.
Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.

items.title: EU sanctions package intended to ‘keep pressure’ on Russia and ‘strike harder’ at its ability to fund Ukraine war – as it happened
items.content:
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen sets out 22nd package of sanctions
Turning to Ukraine, Nato’s Rutte stresses the need to secure the flow of “crucial supplies” or air defence weapons and ammunition to Ukraine.
“
It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete.
We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.”
“Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.”
“One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.”
“It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. …
The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted,
that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and
therefore we must step up to the plate, to ensure that, we stay ahead of danger.”
“But if we are serious about keeping our alliance strong and secure, then
all allies must pull their weight not only in 2035, but starting now.
At least, everybody needs to have the credible path to get there.”
“These investments are also a boon to prosperity. There are dividends to be gained from investing more in defence. This is about real jobs for real people.”

items.title: Iran says it will use all available tools to confront US naval blockade
items.content:
DUBAI, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Iran will use all available tools to confront the US naval blockade, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said in a weekly news conference on Monday.
The blockade on Iran-related oil exports was imposed on April 13, lifted in June after Washington reached a draft understanding with Tehran, then restored on July 14 after the agreement collapsed.
(Reporting by Elwely Elwelly; Editing by Andrew Cawthorne)

items.title: Constitutional law expert brands defence bill allowing secret security rules ‘lazy and irresponsible’
items.content:

Get our
daily political email

free app
or
daily news podcast
Labor’s new defence bill is “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking, one of Australia’s leading constitutional scholars has warned, claiming provisions for the government to secretly class any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues.
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, claimed on Monday that critics of the
“accelerating capability and protecting bases” bill
were “jump[ing] at shadows”, accusing them of “absurd” claims. But parliamentary crossbenchers opposed to the bill, which was rushed through parliament with little public scrutiny, were joined on Monday by Prof Anne Twomey, who expressed alarm about what she called an increasing trend of ministers exercising discretionary powers without parliamentary oversight.

items.title: Morning update
items.content:
Morning update
Good morning Middle East Eye readers,
Here are the latest developments:
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said that Tehran can "act very quickly" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, granted that the US complies with the country's demands. "Iran remains steadfast in honouring its commitments and will fulfil them as soon as possible, provided the other side complies with the relevant conditions," Baqaei said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is urging Trump to carry out strikes on Iran "as soon as possible", according to Israel’s public broadcaster Kan. The report, published on Sunday, indicated that Trump has yet to make a decision on the matter is reluctant to do so.
US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections. Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange". He also questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"
A Saudi attack on Yemen's key port city of Hodeida killed at least four people and injured 18 others, according to Houthi-affiliated media. The strike reportedly targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation.
South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Instead, he cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

items.title: From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
items.content:
From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
In a series of coordinated attacks across several villages near the city of Ramallah in the central occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers torched Palestinian vehicles between Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
The settlers also spray-painted racist slogans on the walls of homes in the three villages, calling for the killing of Arabs and for revenge against them.
Rafat Abu Musa, head of the village council of Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah, told Middle East Eye that settlers infiltrated the southern part of the village at 11.30pm on Saturday and burned down two vehicles.
They spray-painted slogans in Hebrew on the walls of nearby houses, he said, adding that the same area had been targeted by a similar attack two months ago, during which a vehicle was set on fire.
Abu Musa indicated that the settlers came from a newly built outpost on the summit of Jabal al-Ras, located in the neighbouring village of Umm Safa.

Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah

items.title: Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?
items.content:
In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions
Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.
That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.

items.title: Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing
items.content:
Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing
Dr Amina Shareef, a researcher of anti-Muslim racism, says that the destruction unfolding in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon is part of a longer history of anti-Muslim racism that has made mass Muslim suffering and death politically permissible.
She says that Islamophobia is not simply a matter of prejudice or discrimination, but a global system of racial power that constructs Muslims and those identified as Muslim as security threats, allowing violence against them to be justified in the name of security.
Central to this system is the figure of the Muslim terrorist, which portrays Muslim political agency as inherently threatening. Shareef says that this logic extends beyond surveillance, detention and militarised borders to warfare, political abandonment and the destruction of the conditions necessary for life.
She identifies Palestine as a key site where contemporary security practices and technologies of control have been refined and reproduced elsewhere, a process she describes through the concept of the “Palestine boomerang”. Although conflicts in Iran, Lebanon, Kashmir, Syria, Yemen, Iraq and Afghanistan have distinct histories, she argues that they reveal a recurring pattern in which Muslim populations are portrayed as threats and their suffering becomes easier to justify.
Shareef concludes that confronting anti-Muslim racism is ultimately a struggle to protect life and human dignity. She calls for sustained resistance to systems that expose entire populations to premature death, arguing that the responsibility to seek justice remains even when the outcome is uncertain.

items.title: Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
items.content:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections.
"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his platform Truth Social.
Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".
"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed.
Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".
In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"

items.title: Fewer than half in UK will pay TV licence fee within a decade, report warns
items.content:
Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’
Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a
“spiral of decline”
.
With senior BBC figures
concerned about the accelerating fall
in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.

أوكرانيا: مقتل 13 شخصا على الأقل بضربات روسية في محيط كييف وانهيار جزئي لمبنى سكني
أسفرت ضربات روسية على بلدات في منطقة كييف عن مقتل 13 شخصا على الأقل، بينهم امرأة وشاب، وإصابة 15 آخرين، وفق السلطات الأوكرانية. وتسببت إحدى الضربات في انهيار جزء من مبنى سكني في بلدة ديمر، حيث تمكنت فرق الإنقاذ من انتشال طفل حيا، فيما تواصل البحث عن مفقودين تحت الأنقاض. وتأتي الهجمات مع تكثيف روسيا ضرباتها على منشآت الطاقة الأوكرانية واقتراب فصل الشتاء.

items.title: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find
items.content:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’
Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.
Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

items.title: Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
items.content:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - As the COP31 climate conference drifted into what proved to be record overtime, a negotiator from a small island state complained that a promised meeting with the talks' Turkish and Australian presidents had been cancelled yet again.
Saudi officials, meanwhile, had regular access, allowing them disproportionate influence at the Antalya conference, according to negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa.

items.title: Video of ICE detaining father and daughter while boarding flight sparks protests in Seattle
items.content:
Footage of Saturday incident, filmed by fellow passengers, quickly went viral on social media as mayor calls tactics ‘un-American’
Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on Sunday after widely shared footage captured masked immigration agents detaining a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge as they boarded their Alaska Airlines flight.
Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.

items.title: South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
items.content:
South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The minister told lawmakers that the deployment was not indirect military participation in the conflict, but instead cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

items.title: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
items.content:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.
Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.
"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.
The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.
Read more:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?

items.title: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
items.content:
Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages.
Footage from Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik on Sunday shows burnt-out cars and graffiti reading "Death to Arabs" and "Revenge" painted on walls. Residents said settlers attacked their villages while families were asleep, leaving multiple vehicles destroyed.
"We were sleeping and not expecting that herds of settlers will attack our homes while people are sleeping, we never expected this," said Muneer Alkhatib, a resident of Deir Abu Mashal.
Another resident, Montaser Almalki, said the attackers came from a nearby settler outpost and warned that his family could have been caught in a fire had they not woken up.
The attacks took place across several locations in the occupied West Bank. They were condemned by Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who described them as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging the violence.

items.title: Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
items.content:
Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
Israeli
forces detonated explosives to destroy structures on the outskirts of Qantara in southern
Lebanon
, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported.
Earlier on Sunday, Israeli forces set off a massive explosion in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, followed by another in Kfar Tibnit, according to NNA.
The blasts could be heard across much of southern Lebanon.
Residents of Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Zawtar held two separate protests against the Lebanese government's "silence" over Israel's occupation of areas up to the Litani River, which began in March, according to NNA.
Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said he would not accept congratulations on Lebanon's Independence Day, which falls on 22 November, in solidarity with residents of the occupied southern border villages.
In a statement, Berri described this year's independence as "incomplete and unfulfilled".
He said it would be complete only once Lebanese territory was liberated and official and popular positions were united again.

items.title: Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
items.content:
Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks by settlers in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism", accusing far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir of fuelling violence against Palestinians.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages near Ramallah, setting fire to vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, described the attacks as "Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word" and called on the government and security establishment to take tougher action against violent settlers.
"The acts of sabotage carried out by extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes undermine regional stability, endanger lives and seriously harm Israel's national security and foreign relations," he
wrote
on X.
Opposition leader Yair Lapid also
condemned
the attacks, calling them "Jewish terrorism" caused by government negligence.
"Jewish terrorism is the product of criminal negligence on the part of the Israeli government," Lapid said. "By remaining silent, government ministers are deliberately encouraging these pogroms."
"When we form a government, we will tackle this terrorism and restore governance, law and order," he added.
In the United States, Democratic Congressman Josh Gottheimer condemned the attacks and called for accountability.
"These incidents warrant a full and thorough investigation," Gottheimer
wrote
on X, adding that vigilante justice had "no place" in society.
Israeli police said they had opened investigations into arson, vandalism and property damage.

items.title: Analysis-Can climate diplomacy build on the collapse of COP31?
items.content:
By Peter Hobson, Simon Jessop, Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.
For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual UN conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.

items.title: Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
items.content:
Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids and attacks across the occupied West Bank on Sunday, injuring and detaining Palestinians, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. The attacks come amid a sharp escalation in settler violence in the territory.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages,
setting fire
to 12 vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
The attacks targeted Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, in the Ramallah and al-Bireh governorate.
Near Hizma, north-east of Jerusalem, Israeli forces fired live ammunition at
Palestinian workers
trying to cross the separation wall into the city, wounding several of them, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.
Around 18 workers were detained, and video footage showed one of them being severely beaten.
The Palestine Red Crescent said it treated two people who were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces and falling from the wall. Israeli forces later closed the entrances to Hizma and forced shops to shut.
In al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, several Palestinians were injured by flying glass when settlers attacked vehicles on Sunday evening, the head of the village council, Amin Abu Alia, told Wafa.
Abu Alia said settlers, protected by Israeli forces, gathered at the village entrances and
prevented
residents from entering or leaving. He added that Israeli forces detained several Palestinians, and that there was no information so far on their fate or whereabouts.
Many Palestinian residents were also left stranded in the neighbouring village of Abu Falah, unable to return home.
South of Jenin, Israeli forces raided the towns of Anza, Jaba', Arraba and Ya'bad.
Video footage
showed Palestinian man severely beaten by Israeli soldiers inside his house in Ya'bad.
In Azzun Atma, south of Qalqilya, Israeli forces demolished a Palestinian family home of around 120 square metres and a poultry farm, the village council said.
In the northern Jordan Valley, Israeli settlers ploughed around 50 dunams of Palestinian-owned land in the al-Farsiya area.
Palestinian man inspects the burnt-out vehicles following an attack by Israeli settlers, in Kafr Malik near the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, 22 November 2026 (Zain Jaafar/AFP)

their recent meeting
in China.
Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. posted a photo of himself and Putin
shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”

items.title: تركيا: آلاف المتظاهرين في إسطنبول احتجاجا على التضييق على وسائل الإعلام المعارضة
items.content:
تركيا: آلاف المتظاهرين في إسطنبول احتجاجا على التضييق على وسائل الإعلام المعارضة
تظاهر آلاف الأشخاص، الأحد، في مدينة إسطنبول التركية احتجاجا على تصاعد الإجراءات التي تستهدف وسائل الإعلام المؤيدة للمعارضة، وذلك بعد أيام من مداهمة الشرطة مقر قناة "سوزجو" ومجموعتها الإعلامية، وتوقيف عدد من العاملين فيها وتعيين وصي حكومي لإدارتها، في خطوة أثارت مخاوف متزايدة بشأن حرية الصحافة في البلاد.

👈 اقرأ المزيد: https://f24.my/CIh4.g
